result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is built on one stated idea (the L as a ledger column on its rule), uses a tight navy-and-brass palette, and shows a full system: stacked, reversed, one-color and small-size versions, plus clear-space rules. A is restrained too, with a serif wordmark and a monogram that adds a larkspur spike, but it brings back the old purple and teal and its mark has more detail. Neither visible screenshot prints 'Established 1998' or explains why an invented date is a problem, and the business card and signature fall below the visible area in both, so items 2–4 are only partly verifiable. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Only the top of each page is visible, so the business cards, email signatures and any note about the founding date can't be checked. In what shows, A's mark is the more restrained and confident of the two: one idea (the L as a ledger column on its rule), navy with one brass accent, and black and small-size versions. B's mark stacks a serif L, a dotted larkspur stalk and an inset border, and its five-colour palette still leans on the old purple and teal, so it looks less settled. Neither visible area prints 'Established 1998', but neither visibly explains why a made-up date is a bad idea.
